relationships.description: The instrumentation entry switches on telemetry capture for the libraries or code paths inside a service or module, so the component's requests, calls and errors become observable as spans, metrics and logs.
relationships.evidence: The component's SDK bootstrap registers the auto-instrumentation plugin (e.g. a NodeSDK instrumentations array or a Java agent config), or its source obtains a Tracer and wraps its own methods in manual spans.

relationships.description: The instrumentation entry captures telemetry for a client-side router entry, recording route changes, render or lazy-load timing and errors when the browser location matches that path pattern.
relationships.evidence: The front-end telemetry bootstrap registers a router or document-load instrumentation (e.g. a browser auto-instrumentation plugin or a router navigation hook calling tracer.startSpan) that tags spans with the route's path pattern.

relationships.description: The instrumentation entry traces the application's interactions with a third-party platform product such as a database engine, message broker or cache server, exposing query, publish or cache-call latency and failures.
relationships.evidence: The SDK configuration enables the client-library instrumentation for that product (e.g. pg, redis, kafka or JDBC instrumentation), and emitted spans carry db.system or messaging.system attributes naming it.

relationships.description: The instrumentation entry points to the exporter configuration through which the telemetry it enables is expected to leave the process, without itself defining endpoint or protocol.
relationships.evidence: The instrumentation entry in the telemetry configuration file or bootstrap code names the exporter by identifier, or both are wired into the same TracerProvider or MeterProvider setup.

relationships.description: The choice of which libraries are instrumented and how complies with a recorded restriction, such as a mandate to use OpenTelemetry, a ban on capturing request bodies, or a ceiling on instrumentation overhead.
relationships.evidence: An architecture decision record or policy states the restriction and the instrumentation config visibly conforms to it, e.g. using only OTel instrumentations or disabling payload capture options it forbids.

relationships.description: The instrumentation entry supplies the named producer identity under which the enabled library or manual code obtains its Tracer, Meter or Logger, so emitted signals are tagged with that scope.
relationships.evidence: The instrumentation plugin's constructor or the manual site calls getTracer/getMeter/getLogger with the scope name and version, which appears as otel.scope.name on exported data.

relationships.description: The telemetry captured by the instrumentation entry is emitted through providers that attach the process's resource attributes, making the instrumentation a contributor of signals attributed to that service, host or container identity.
relationships.evidence: The same SDK bootstrap that registers the instrumentation constructs the Resource (via OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES, resource detectors or code) and passes it to the provider the instrumentation uses.

notes: references exporterconfig conflicts with the source definition excluding where telemetry is sent; the link is indirect via providers. serves resource is weak: the Resource is per-process and attached by providers, not served by an instrumentation entry. serves instrumentationscope is closer to 'uses' or 'generates' than serving.
